doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

chapter: New Zealand and the road to jazz
title: Taking a boat to New York and Berklee at nineteen
summary: He says leaving New Zealand was a compulsion not shared by peers; he took a month-long boat trip, supported by his parents, to attend Berklee on a small scholarship.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did musicians that rose to a certain level of notoriety in New Zealand, especially in the jazz world, was there a feeling that we need to go, as you put it, thousands of miles away to where this music came from? Was that a goal for most people?

No. And it wasn’t a goal for me, it was a compunction. It was — something grabbed ahold of me. It didn’t grab ahold of any of my peers. And I got on a boat, damn it. I got on a boat for 300 pounds, a four berth cabin down below sea level. And I was on that boat for a month to get to New York etcetera etcetera. So when I look back on it I’m going what!? Because I couldn’t afford a plane, and planes had to hop, skip and a jump
over to Hawaii and then stop somewhere in L.A. and then another stop just to get to New York. So I figured it was easier to just get a boat and get off at the other end.
Did your parents see you off on that boat?
Oh yeah. And I’m eternally grateful to them for letting me go you know. I was 19. 19.
Do you recall if you had a destination like you knew a person or —
Yes, well I was going to Berklee College, Berklee School of Music. I got a small scholarship which sort of got me in and got me a student visa, and the rest is history.
